Synopsis:
Players can use Speak with Animals to talk to the pigeon at the Post house to find out more information regarding the missing letters. The pigeon will point the player towards the Open Hand Temple roof.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_Posthouse_Pigeon.json: You’ve used Speak with Animals (or a similar effect) to question the messenger pigeon loitering at the Post House about a set of missing letters; the bird is officious, wants a terse “report” about a recent skirmish, and notes that several of its fliers never returned. Off‑screen, those carrier birds disappeared during or after a nearby battle, and the pigeon directs you toward the Open Hand Temple roof as the likeliest place to recover the lost correspondence. The temple itself is already tense — priests are arguing about Father Lorgan’s murder and refugee politics — so any investigation on the roof may intersect with that dispute and influence how locals react. Depending on your prior actions, roof access or movement there can also be limited (for example by Steel Watchers or other forces), so you may encounter guards or obstacles when following the pigeon’s lead.
- WYR_Posthouse_PAD_PlayerSpotsPigeonBlood000.json: Player passes a nature check and identifies the first sign of the missing pigeons.
- WYR_MerchantsHouse_Merchant.json: The scene takes place after the Rivington Rats have left or a merchant‑conflict was just ended, with the player confronting Arfur Gregorio about explosive toy bears he’s implicated in donating to refugees. Arfur is frantic and desperate — insisting he was forced or framed, terrified of powerful city figures (and of being killed or imprisoned), and offering a bribe (a pass granting Lower City access) to make you go away. The player’s choices determine whether he’s spared, arrested, or killed; his lines alternate between panicked denials and pleas for mercy. Off‑screen, the player has just disturbed a nearby windmill (flinging a small gnome) and drawn goblin scouts away to investigate, and the player may also be holding the Moonlantern/pixie, a separate moral dilemma that colors the encounter.
- WYR_Posthouse_CourierDog.json: speak to courier dog at posthouse once the situation is resolved
- WYR_VampireSpawns_OM_Astarion_AOM_OOM.json: Dalyria and Petras at the flophouse.They are looking for Astarion at the place where they used to "hunt".This is a dialog for when they meet Astarion-Avatar or Astarion-Companion with the player-Avatar.They will tell Astarion they must inform Cazador that Astarion is back in the city. They will also reveal that Cazador is planning a ritual that requires all the spawn and that will grant them new powers.If Astarion knows that Cazador is actually planning to sacrifice all the spawn, he might be able to convince the spawn about this sacrifice. In exchange, they will reveal a bit of information about Cazador's Palace.After the dialog, they disappear as clouds of mist.

- Pigeon: Make your report. How did the battle unfold? || [context] NodeContext: Clipped, commanding (node 22)
- Player: They died horrible, painful deaths. Blood, guts and feathers all over the place. (node 66)

context: You're speaking with the messenger pigeon at the Post House via Speak with Animals to learn about a cache of missing letters. The bird is officious and demands a terse "report" about a recent skirmish in which several carrier pigeons disappeared; off‑screen those fliers vanished during or after the nearby battle. The pigeon directs you to the Open Hand Temple roof as the likeliest place to recover the lost correspondence, but the temple is already tense—priests are arguing about Father Lorgan’s murder and refugee politics—so investigating the roof may intersect with that dispute. Depending on your earlier actions (and checks you may have passed, such as spotting pigeon blood), roof access or movement there can be restricted by guards or other obstacles.
